transcript.content: Good day. What brings you in today?

Good day. Um… I guess I’m here because I’ve just been really tired lately. I mean, I’m functioning, I’m still getting to work and doing what I need to do, but it feels harder than it should. Sleep doesn’t really seem to fix it, and by the time I get through a normal workday and dinner at home, I’m just… exhausted. I’m not sure if that’s the sort of thing to come in for, but it’s been wearing on me.
Have you noticed any changes in your mood lately, like feeling down or losing interest in things you usually enjoy?

Yeah… I mean, I don’t want to make it sound too dramatic, but most days lately I wake up with this kind of heavy, gray feeling. Like I’m already disappointed in the day before it’s even really started, if that makes sense. It’s not that I can’t do things, I do, but my mood has definitely felt lower than usual.
Have you found that things you usually enjoy, like hobbies or spending time with friends, feel less pleasurable or interesting lately?

Yes… I think so. I mean, not completely, I don’t want to overstate it, but I usually really love painting, and I like going to museum exhibits when I can. Lately my paints are just sitting there untouched, and when I think about going to a museum I sort of… can’t make myself care enough to go. It feels silly saying it, but it’s definitely different for me.
Would you say that your tiredness or exhaustion is something new or more severe than what you normally feel, even when you haven’t been doing much physically or mentally demanding?

Yes… I think it is more than my usual tired, though I keep wondering if I’m making too much of it. It’s not like I’m doing anything extreme physically, but even a normal workday and then just getting through dinner at home feels heavier than it should. And sleeping doesn’t really seem to reset me the way it normally would.
Would you say that this heavy or low mood you’re describing has been present most of the day, nearly every day, lately?

Yes… I think that’s fair to say. I don’t want to make it sound like I’m miserable every single second, but most days lately I wake up with that heavy, gray feeling, like I’m already disappointed in the day before it even starts. It tends to hang around for a lot of the day.
Would you say you’ve been feeling a loss of energy or increased fatigue nearly every day, even when you haven’t been doing much physically or mentally demanding?

Yes… I think so. I don’t want to make it sound dramatic, but that’s actually a big part of why I came in. I’m just exhausted in this way that sleep doesn’t really fix. Even when I haven’t done anything especially demanding, just getting through a normal workday and then dinner at home feels… heavier than it should, if that makes sense.
Have you noticed any changes in your appetite or weight lately, like eating more or less than usual or losing or gaining weight without trying?

A little, yes… I mean, nothing dramatic, I don’t think. I’ve just been sort of picking at meals, and at work I sometimes realize I forgot to eat lunch. And a couple of my skirts are fitting a bit looser, even though I’m not trying to lose weight. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Have you found yourself feeling more guilty or worthless lately, like you’re a failure or that you’re letting people down, even when you know it might not be true?

Yes… I mean, I try not to wallow in it, and I know logically I’m probably being harder on myself than I’d be on anyone else. But I do keep replaying things — like family plans I missed, or conversations with my husband where I was tense or short — and then I start feeling like I’m letting everyone down.

It’s not that I think I’m a terrible person exactly, but I feel like I’m not doing a good enough job as a wife, or a mother, or even at work as a manager. I don’t know if that counts as guilt in the way you mean, but it’s been there.
Have you noticed that you're moving more slowly than usual, or maybe fidgety and restless lately — something that other people might notice?

Maybe a little… I wasn’t sure if it counted. I don’t think I’m, you know, noticeably dragging myself around or anything. But my staff has mentioned that in meetings I’m slower to answer questions than usual — like there’s this pause before I can get my thoughts together and actually say the words. I hope that makes sense.
Have you had episodes like this before, where you felt persistently down or exhausted for a prolonged period of time, or is this the first time you’ve experienced something like this?

Yes… I think so. This isn’t the first time, though I guess I’ve always tried to tell myself it was just stress or being tired.

The longest stretch I can clearly remember was about five months where I felt low and worn out most days, and just… not really like myself. It wasn’t like I couldn’t function at all, so maybe I didn’t take it as seriously as I should have, but it did go on for quite a while. Does that answer what you mean?
Before the five-month period you mentioned, have you had any other distinct periods where you felt persistently down or exhausted for several weeks or more?

I’m not sure I can point to another clear one before that. There were times I’d say I was tired or stressed, but I don’t know that they lasted several weeks in the way you mean.

I don’t want to give you the wrong answer — I just can’t remember anything as distinct as that five-month stretch.
Since that five-month period, have you had any other episodes where you felt persistently down or exhausted for several weeks or more?

Since then… yes, I think this current one would count. It hasn’t been as long as that five-month stretch, but for about a month now I’ve had this swing from being unusually energized and driven into feeling pretty low and worn out most days.

I don’t want to overstate it, but it has been persistent enough that I’ve noticed it. Is that the kind of episode you mean?
Would you say the periods of being unusually energized and driven, which you mentioned, included feeling like your thoughts were racing, needing less sleep, or being more talkative than usual?

Yes… I think the racing thoughts part, definitely, though I don’t know if I would’ve called it that at the time.

It was more like my mind had too many tabs open at once — ideas for work, things for the cultural group, our household schedule — all sort of running through my head together. I could still manage, mostly, so I told myself it was just being productive, but it did feel hard to quiet down. Does that make sense?
Before the five-month period you mentioned, have you ever had a distinct period of at least two weeks where you felt persistently down or lost interest in most things, almost every day?

Before that five-month period… I don’t think I can say there was a clear two-week stretch like that.

Lately, yes, most days I wake up with this heavy, gray feeling — like I’m already disappointed in the day before it even starts. But before that longer period, I honestly can’t remember anything that distinct. I’m sorry, I’m trying to answer it the right way.

Have you ever had a period of at least four days where you felt unusually high, overly confident, or irritable — not just happy because something good happened, but more like a sustained, intense mood that stood out from how you usually feel?

I think… yes, earlier this month there was a stretch like that. I wouldn’t say I was out of control or anything, but I felt unusually charged and upbeat, like I was suddenly brilliant and could handle everything.

And then if my husband questioned one of my plans, I’d get irritated really quickly. More quickly than I’d like to admit. I’m not proud of that, but it did feel noticeably different from my usual mood.
Have you had more than one period in your life where you felt unusually high, overly confident, or irritable for several days in a row, where this mood was clearly different from your usual self?

More than one… I’m not sure I can honestly say that. The one that stands out is earlier this month, when I felt unusually charged and upbeat — like I was suddenly brilliant and could handle everything — and then I’d get irritated really fast if my husband questioned my plans.

There may have been milder times, but I don’t want to overstate it. That recent stretch is the one I can clearly point to.

Have you had at least two separate periods in your life where your mood changed significantly and lasted for days or longer — one being the recent period you described where you felt unusually high and then low?

I think… if I’m understanding you right, the clearest separate longer period was the low one. The longest depressed stretch I can really point to lasted about five months, where I felt low and tired and just not like myself most days.

And then the recent few days where I felt unusually up — that would be the other kind of change. I’m saying that carefully because I don’t want to make it sound more dramatic than it was, but yes, those are the two I can clearly describe.

Can you recall if you’ve had at least two separate times in your life where you felt unusually high, irritable, or overly confident for several days in a row — times that were clearly different from your usual mood and not just a reaction to something good happening?

I’m honestly not sure about two separate times. The one I keep coming back to is earlier this month — I had this really charged, upbeat feeling, like I was… I don’t know, unusually confident, like my ideas were brilliant. And then I’d get irritated pretty quickly if my husband questioned what I was planning.

I don’t want to exaggerate it or make it sound worse than it was, but that period was definitely different from my usual mood.

Can you recall if you’ve had at least two separate times in your life where you felt unusually high, overly confident, or irritable for several days in a row — not just a reaction to something good happening, but a mood that really stood out from how you usually feel?

I don’t think I can clearly say there were two. The one I can point to is earlier this month — I had this unusually charged, upbeat mood, like I felt brilliant and really sure of my plans, and then I’d get irritated fast if my husband questioned me.

I’m trying not to overstate it, but that one did stand out from how I usually am.

There may have been milder times, but I don’t want to overstate it. That recent stretch is the one I can clearly point to.

inference.note: This turn added confirmation of a second episode of depression (current episode) and a recent hypomanic episode. This supports the diagnosis of Bipolar I Disorder, which requires at least one manic or hypomanic episode in addition to depressive episodes. However, since the patient has only one clearly described hypomanic episode so far, the Bipolar II vs. Bipolar I remains uncertain, hence all F31 codes remain in play.

patient.answer:
I think… if I’m understanding you right, the clearest separate longer period was the low one. The longest depressed stretch I can really point to lasted about five months, where I felt low and tired and just not like myself most days.

And then the recent few days where I felt unusually up — that would be the other kind of change. I’m saying that carefully because I don’t want to make it sound more dramatic than it was, but yes, those are the two I can clearly describe.

inference.note: This turn ruled out having multiple distinct manic episodes (at least two), which reduces the likelihood of higher severity Bipolar I Disorder codes (F31.7-F31.9). It confirms a single manic-like episode along with a major depressive episode, supporting the lower-range F31 codes. The diagnosis remains uncertain, so it is not yet final.

patient.answer:
